record.title: Epistemic Superposition as the Mechanistic Signature of LLM Hallucination: Cross-Layer SAE Activation-Entropy Monitoring and Consistency Enforcement for Inference-Time Hallucination Reduction
record.statement: When LLMs hallucinate, the feed-forward key-value memory modules at factual-retrieval transformer layers (roughly layers 40–70% of total depth) partially activate multiple semantically competing, mutually-exclusive factual SAE features simultaneously — a state of *epistemic superposition* measurable as anomalously high Shannon entropy over sparse-autoencoder feature activations — and enforcing cross-layer SAE feature-cluster consistency by progressively concentrating this distribution toward the dominant competing feature at inference time will causally reduce hallucination rates across TruthfulQA, HaluEval, and FactScore without requiring labeled hallucination training data.
record.mechanism:
The proposed mechanism rests on the intersection of two established findings: (1) feed-forward networks in transformers act as key-value memories that store factual associations (Dai et al., 2022), and (2) SAEs decompose residual stream activations into interpretable, monosemantic features via overcomplete sparse representation (survey background). 

When generating a factual claim the model knows with high confidence, the FFN at the relevant layer performs a near-lookup: the query (current residual stream) strongly matches a single stored key, producing a high-magnitude, concentrated output that projects the residual stream onto a small set of highly-activated SAE features — low Shannon entropy H_SAE. 

When the model lacks sufficient training exposure to a queried fact (or when the fact is confounded by similar but incorrect training examples), the FFN query partially matches multiple competing keys simultaneously. This produces a superimposed output that simultaneously activates SAE features corresponding to several related but mutually-exclusive factual entities (e.g., multiple capital cities, multiple birth years, multiple authors). The resulting SAE activation distribution has anomalously high entropy H_SAE — the model is in a state of *epistemic superposition*.

Critically, this unresolved superposition explains the cross-layer coherence reported by Rateike et al. (2024): because no subsequent attention pattern can reliably distinguish which factual feature is correct (there is no grounding signal within the forward pass), the competing feature set propagates forward largely intact through successive transformer blocks. Each layer's FFN and attention components further process the mixed residual stream without resolving the ambiguity, leading to coherent but unresolved superposition across many layers — manifesting as the observed cross-layer persistence of hallucination-associated features.

The intervention exploits this structure in three stages:

(A) **Layer-wise H_SAE monitoring**: At each forward pass, compute the Shannon entropy of the SAE activation magnitudes H_SAE(l) at candidate factual-retrieval layers l. A threshold τ (calibrated on held-out factual queries with known ground truth) identifies when a forward pass enters epistemic superposition.

(B) **Dominant-feature concentration (DFC) intervention**: When H_SAE(l) > τ, apply a sparse concentration operation to the residual stream: identify the top-k SAE features by activation magnitude (the model's 'best guess' factual representation), suppress all other competing features via targeted residual stream subtraction (projecting out their associated decoder directions), and amplify the top-k feature directions proportionally to restore reconstruction fidelity. This resolves the superposition toward the model's highest-confidence factual representation.

(C) **Cross-layer consistency enforcement (CLCE)**: Require that the feature identity of the top-k active features at layer l remains a subset of the top-2k features at layer l+1. When drift is detected (indicating spreading, unresolvable superposition), apply DFC again at l+1. This propagation-aware intervention prevents cascading entropy growth across subsequent layers.

Alternatively, when the model has no dominant competing feature (all SAE features are activated at similarly low magnitude, indicating near-total ignorance), both DFC and CLCE can instead amplify a pre-identified 'epistemic uncertainty' SAE feature cluster — identified from labeled examples of honest 'I don't know' outputs — to elicit calibrated uncertainty expression rather than hallucinated content.

The mechanistic grounding is specific: hallucination arises not because a single wrong feature is active (as in Rateike et al.'s framing of 'hallucination features'), but because the FFN fails to commit the residual stream to any single factual feature, producing a thermodynamically disordered SAE activation state. The intervention is causally effective because it restores the ordered, low-entropy state that characterises the model's behaviour when it possesses confident factual knowledge.
entities: Shannon entropy over SAE feature activations
record.anticipated_outcomes:
If the hypothesis is correct, the following quantitative and qualitative observations should hold:

1. **H_SAE discriminates hallucinations**: At factual-retrieval layers (identified by probing or known from prior work), H_SAE computed on the SAE decomposition of the residual stream will be significantly higher for hallucinated outputs than for factually correct outputs (ROC-AUC > 0.75 on TruthfulQA and HaluEval), and this discrimination will be achievable without any labeled hallucination training data — only a threshold calibrated on a small held-out factual set.

2. **DFC reduces hallucination rates**: Applying the dominant-feature concentration intervention when H_SAE > τ will reduce TruthfulQA accuracy improvements by ≥ 10% (matching or exceeding Rateike et al.'s 10% cap), while extending improvements to HaluEval (hallucination detection F1) and FactScore (precision of factual claims).

3. **CLCE provides additive benefit**: Adding cross-layer consistency enforcement on top of DFC will yield a further reduction in hallucination rate (≥ 3–5% additional TruthfulQA improvement) by preventing superposition from re-emerging after initial concentration.

4. **Cross-layer coherence explained**: The SAE features active in the high-entropy state at layer l will remain among the top-2k active features at layers l+1 through l+5, confirming that unresolved epistemic superposition is the mechanism of cross-layer coherence (quantified by Jaccard similarity of top-k feature sets across layers: J > 0.6 for hallucinated outputs, J < 0.3 for correct outputs).

5. **Human-interpretable competing features**: Qualitative analysis of the SAE features co-active during high H_SAE states will reveal semantically coherent clusters of competing facts (e.g., multiple named entities of the same type), confirming that the model is representing genuinely competing factual candidates rather than noise.

6. **Generalization across model families**: The H_SAE signal and DFC/CLCE interventions will generalise across Llama, Mistral, and Gemma model families with consistent (if quantitatively varying) hallucination reduction, since the FFN key-value memory mechanism is shared across all transformer architectures.

7. **Minimal side effects**: DFC and CLCE will not degrade performance on non-hallucination benchmarks (e.g., MMLU, HellaSwag) by more than 1–2%, consistent with prior demonstration of minimal side effects from SAE-based feature suppression (O'Brien et al., 2024).
record.novelty_argument:
This hypothesis is novel along four distinct dimensions relative to the cited literature:

1. **Mechanistic explanation of cross-layer coherence**: Rateike et al. (2024) observe and exploit cross-layer coherent hallucination features but explicitly leave open the question of why this coherence arises. This hypothesis provides a specific mechanistic answer — unresolved epistemic superposition from partial FFN key-value memory activation — grounding the empirical observation in a causal, compositional account of transformer computations.

2. **Entropy as an unsupervised hallucination signal**: Rateike et al. identify hallucination features via supervised differential frequency analysis (requiring labeled hallucinating vs. non-hallucinating examples). This hypothesis proposes that the distributional property of SAE feature activations — their Shannon entropy H_SAE — is itself the primary, unsupervised hallucination indicator. This is conceptually distinct: it characterizes the *state* of the SAE decomposition rather than the identity of specific features, enabling zero-shot generalization to new domains and model families without labeled hallucination data.

3. **Cross-layer consistency enforcement (CLCE) as a novel intervention**: Prior SAE-based interventions (Rateike et al., O'Brien et al., Quirke) operate at a single layer by suppressing pre-identified features. CLCE is a structurally different, propagation-aware intervention that monitors and enforces consistency of the dominant SAE feature cluster across adjacent transformer layers, preventing cascading entropy growth. This leverages the unique multi-layer structure of SAEs in a way not previously proposed.

4. **Multi-benchmark generalization as a design criterion**: Rateike et al. validate exclusively on TruthfulQA. This hypothesis explicitly targets generalization to HaluEval (model-generated hallucinations in diverse QA tasks) and FactScore (open-domain biographical generation), both of which stress different hallucination mechanisms (multi-hop reasoning vs. long-form generation) and will provide a more complete empirical picture. The unsupervised entropy signal is specifically motivated by the need to transfer across these diverse domains without retraining.

The hypothesis goes well beyond naive probing classifiers (which would only correlate with hallucination) or linear probes (which lack the fine-grained feature decomposition needed for the CLCE intervention), exploiting the unique sparse, interpretable, overcomplete structure that SAEs provide — specifically their ability to simultaneously identify *which* competing factual representations are active and *how concentrated* the activation distribution is.
